name: Lake Ala-Kul
near: Karakol — ~20 km as the crow flies to the north; the trek starts from the Karakol gorge (the entrance to the Karakol nature park, ~10 km from the town) or from Altyn-Arashan (the village of Ak-Suu/Teplokluchenka — the marshrutka (minibus) terminus). The OSM marker “Lesnoye” at 17 km is technical; the approach does not go through it.
elev: The lake 3532 m (advantour, eurasia.travel; 3500–3560 m in blogs); Ala-Kul Pass 3860 m (up to 3900–3990 m in some guides); Sirota camp ~2800 m; the mountaineering camp/entrance to the Karakol gorge ~2600 m.
short: Ala-Kul (“motley lake”) is a glacial lake at 3532 m in the Terskey Ala-Too, the goal of Kyrgyzstan's most popular trek from Karakol.
desc: Ala-Kul is a high-mountain glacial lake 2.3 km long, up to 700 m wide and more than 70 m deep, dammed by a moraine between the Karakol gorge and the Altyn-Arashan valley. The water is turquoise in clear weather and grey in rain, hence the name “motley lake”. It freezes in late autumn and opens in May. There is no road to the lake — only a 2–4 day walking route ~55 km long from the Karakol gorge via Sirota camp, Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) and the Altyn-Arashan hot springs; a day out-and-back from the mountaineering camp is possible with a 4×4 / SUV drop-off.
guide: The classic is a 3–4 day trek: from the Karakol gorge across a bridge to Sirota camp (2800 m), then a steep climb onto the moraine — and the lake opens suddenly, all at once, with a glacier at the far end. Overnight in yurts by the lake and get up before dawn: in the early morning the water is at its most turquoise, and by lunchtime clouds often roll in. Take Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) in the morning over the scree, trekking poles are a must; from the saddle you can see both the lake and the Altyn-Arashan valley, where you will descend to the hot baths. If you are short of days — order a UAZ to the mountaineering camp and visit the lake as a day out-and-back (about 7 km one way, 4 h up), as local groups do. Sirota has Wi-Fi, beyond that there is no signal — download the track in advance.
see: The turquoise lake with the Takyr-Tor glacier at its head; the panorama from Ala-Kul Pass (3860 m) of the lake and Altyn-Arashan; Sirota camp in the spruce forest; a waterfall on the climb from Sirota; the Altyn-Arashan hot springs (2500 m) and a view of Palatka Peak; the Karakol gorge with Tian Shan spruces.
skip: You have less than 2 full days or no acclimatization — the pass at nearly 3900 m with a daily gain of 1000 m. You are not ready to overnight in a yurt/tent without a shower or mobile signal. You are going before mid-June or after the end of September — the yurt camps are packed up and there is snow on the pass.
diff: Moderate–high: 55 km over 3–4 days, a total ascent of ~2570 m, the hardest day is the climb to the pass (+1000 m, 6–10 h) over scree; altitude up to 3860–3900 m, risk of altitude sickness. A day out-and-back from the mountaineering camp is ~7 km and ~900 m of ascent one way (4 h). Good physical fitness and experience of overnights are required.
when: Late June — mid/late September; best July — early September. The yurt camps operate roughly from 1 July to 15–20 September. The lake is under ice from late autumn to May. The weather is “four seasons in a day”, snow on the pass is possible in any month.
hours: The Karakol nature park — entry through the eco-post in the Karakol gorge in the daytime (hours are not published); the lake is an open area, around the clock. Yurt camps: seasonal, ~1 July — 20 September.
daytime: Dawn and morning at the lake — the purest turquoise and calm, cross the pass in the morning before daytime cloud and thunderstorms; in the evening it is cold and windy at the lake.
how: From Karakol: marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 or a taxi to the entrance of the Karakol nature park (the eco-post in the Karakol gorge), then on foot ~16 km to the Sirota bridge and another ~8–12 km to the lake; or a drop-off by UAZ/GAZ-66 to the mountaineering camp (Ayu-Tor) and an out-and-back. The return is over the pass to Altyn-Arashan and 16 km down to Ak-Suu (marshrutka (minibus) No. 350/501 to Karakol) or by 4×4 / SUV from Altyn-Arashan. From Bishkek to Karakol is ~400 km, marshrutkas (minibuses) from the new bus station (Alma-Atinskaya St. 1/1).
needcar: Only to the start: a marshrutka (minibus)/taxi to the eco-post or a 4×4 / SUV to the mountaineering camp. To the lake and over the pass — only on foot or partly on horseback.
self: Yes — the trail is well trodden and marked, no permits needed (only the park entry fee); many go on their own with a tent or from yurt to yurt. You need a map/GPS track, food for 3–4 days (the camps have food, but it is expensive), and insurance for altitude up to 4000 m.
roadtype: Paved to Karakol; a dirt road in the Karakol gorge to the eco-post and mountaineering camp (passable for a UAZ/4×4 / SUV, in places for passenger cars in dry weather); beyond that only a mountain trail: forest, moraine, scree on the pass. There is no road access to the lake.
traveltime: The classic 4-day trek: day 1 — 12–16 km, 4–5 h to Sirota; day 2 — 8–12 km, 6 h to the lake (+1000 m); day 3 — 10–16 km, 6 h over the pass to Altyn-Arashan; day 4 — 16–18 km, 4–5 h to Ak-Suu. The 3-day option: 18/18/18 km, the second day 9–10 h. The out-and-back from the mountaineering camp: ~7 km, 4 h up, the same down (a group, June 2025). A UAZ drop-off from Karakol to the mountaineering camp ~2 h one way.
stay: Sirota camp (yurts, ~2800 m): 2000 som/person without meals (negotiable), 4200 som with meals (2025); Keldike camp: 2000 som/person without meals (2025); the yurt camp at Lake Ala-Kul: ~$50/person with dinner and breakfast (2025 season); Altyn-Arashan guesthouses: 500–2000 som/person per bed, dinner+breakfast ~450 som, on average ~$45/night with meals (2025); “Elza” in Altyn-Arashan — 4000 som/night with lunch and dinner (2022). Tent: a spot by the lake/Sirota, tent fee ~100 som. In Karakol — dozens of guesthouses and hostels.
net: There is no mobile signal in the Karakol gorge and at the lake (2025 reports); Wi-Fi only at the Sirota hut (paid/by arrangement). In Altyn-Arashan the signal is patchy. Beeline/O!/MegaCom coverage ends at the edge of Karakol.
entry: The Karakol nature park entry fee — the data differ: 100 som/person for CIS citizens (mustvisit.ru, September 2025) and 250–300 som/person at the bridge to Sirota (guides for foreigners, 2024–2025); 500 som per car at the eco-post (June 2025 report); a tent permit ~100 som. Since November 2025 the eco-post tariff is 200 som per passenger car and 800 som per bus/truck (Sputnik, 02.11.2025). Check the 2026 pedestrian tariff on site.
transfer: UAZ Karakol → mountaineering camp and back: 10,000 som for 6 people (June 2025). Taxi Karakol → eco-post 345 som (2025). Marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 — 10–50 som; No. 350 Ak-Suu → Karakol — 40–50 som (2024–2025). An organized trek with a guide, meals and a transfer: €330–530/person for 3–4 days (2026).
bring: A sleeping bag rated to −5 °C (the yurts provide blankets, but it is cold), wind and waterproof gear, a warm layer, trekking poles (a must on the pass), ankle-support boots, a water filter (streams are near grazing), sun protection and sunglasses, cash (only cash in the camps, 8–10 thousand som recommended), a first-aid kit with altitude sickness remedies, a power bank, an offline GPS track.
warn: Altitude up to 3860–3990 m — acclimatize in Karakol/Sirota, descend if a headache is getting worse. The pass is steep scree, with rockfall from people climbing above; poles and a helmet for caution are a must. The weather changes within an hour: snow and thunderstorms in summer. Shepherd dogs at the yurts. Entry fees are collected in cash — the amounts vary, ask for a receipt. The camps close after 15–20 September — out of season only a tent.
food: In the yurts at Sirota and by the lake — dinner of soup/plov/lagman, flatbreads, tea with jam (tea in a yurt ~100 som/person, 2025); in Altyn-Arashan — home cooking at guesthouses, kumis in summer. In Karakol — ashlyan-fu (Dungan cold noodles) at the market, Dungan cuisine, lagman.
reviews: Google Maps (“Ala-Kul”): 4.9/5, 84 ratings as of 03.10.2026. Blogs and forums 2024–2026: pros — one of the most beautiful lakes in the Tian Shan, a good trail, yurts and hot springs at the end; cons — a hard pass and scree, cold and wind at the lake, unpredictable weather, inconsistent entry fees, expensive food in the camps.
p.sum: Only a trail leads to the lake. The classic is a loop of ≈55 km over 3–4 days: the Karakol gorge (marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 or a taxi/UAZ to the bridge) → Sirota camp → the lake → Ala-Kul Pass (3860–3900 m) → the Altyn-Arashan hot springs → Ak-Suu (marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 to Karakol). It is better to go in this direction: the climb to the lake is gentler, and from the pass there is a steep descent over scree. The season is from 1 July to ~20 September, when the yurts operate (Sirota 2500–4500 som with dinner and breakfast, 2025–2026). Without a tent you can go from yurt to yurt; gear can be rented in Karakol.

p.iti.0.title: A day trip (out-and-back)
p.iti.0.plan: 6:00 UAZ from Karakol → 8:00 mountaineering camp → 12:00 the lake (1–1.5 h by the water) → 17:30 mountaineering camp → 19:30 Karakol. Only with good acclimatization.
p.iti.1.title: The classic 3–4 days
p.iti.1.plan: D1: marshrutka (minibus) No. 101 → Karakol valley → Sirota. D2: climb to the lake, a night in a yurt by the lake. D3: the pass in the morning → Altyn-Arashan, bathhouses. D4: on foot/by UAZ to Ak-Suu → marshrutka (minibus) No. 350 to Karakol.
p.iti.2.title: Combinations
p.iti.2.plan: Karakol gorge + Ala-Kul + Altyn-Arashan — one loop; extensions: Altyn-Arashan → Anaarkhar → Jyrgalan or Kok-Zhaiyk → Teleti Pass → the Karakol valley (Jeti-Oguz).
p.season: May–June: the yurts are closed, snow on the trail and the pass, the lake may be under ice until the end of May. 1 July — 20 September: the main season, July–August — the peak (queues at the yurts, book ahead). Late September — October: the camps are packed up, only self-sufficient with a tent, below zero at night. November–April: the lake is under ice, avalanche danger — don't go without winter hiking experience.
p.budget.economy: ≈12,000–16,000 som/person for 3–4 days: marshrutkas (minibuses) No. 101 and No. 350 (≈70 som), park entry 100–300, gear rental ≈2,500 for 4 days (a tent for two — split), your own food ≈2,000, a night at Sirota without food 2,000 or a tent, Elza with breakfast 1,600 + dinner 500, a bathhouse 200.
p.budget.comfort: ≈30,000–45,000 som/person: an organized trek €330–530 (Journal of Nomads) or $310–510 (Nomad's Land) with a guide, meals, transfers and pack horses; or independently with yurts (Sirota 4,500, the lake ≈$50, Altyn-Arashan) + a UAZ to the mountaineering camp and a jeep from Altyn-Arashan (8,000 per vehicle).
p.permits: No border permit needed. Entry to the Karakol nature park is paid: at the eco-post/bridge — 250–300 som/person for foreigners, ≈100 som for CIS (2024–2025), a car — 200 som (since 11.2025); a tent ≈100 som. A descent via Altyn-Arashan — the Karakol forestry fee 20/100/220 som per person (Kyrgyz/CIS/foreigners). Pay in cash, ask for a receipt.
p.access: Children under 12–14 and older people — only with serious preparation (altitude 3900 m, scree). With a stroller — no. With a dog — physically possible, but there are shepherd dogs at the yurts and dogs are unwelcome in the park. An easy alternative for families — a walk in the lower part of the Karakol valley or a UAZ ride to Altyn-Arashan.
